## [0.29.0] - 2026-11-25

### Added

- **PowerShell: code intelligence and debugging.** PowerShell Editor Services (VS Code's PowerShell engine, on `pwsh`)
  is PowerShell's language server — PSScriptAnalyzer's diagnostics, completion, hover, definitions, rename, formatting
  — and its debugger: F5 on a `.ps1` (or a launch.json `PowerShell` configuration) stops at breakpoints with
  PowerShell's scopes in Variables, and the script's output, warnings and errors reach the Debug console. Run File runs
  a script on `pwsh`. Editora finds PSES in its own `plugins/dap/powershell`, at the path in Settings → Debugging, or in
  VS Code's PowerShell extension.
- **C and C++ tests: GoogleTest, Catch2 and doctest.** A C or C++ test file has a ▶ per test and one for the whole
  file. Run File, Run Test at Caret and a test's ▶ build its program and run it with the test's filter
  (`--gtest_filter`, a Catch2 test spec, `--test-case`), into Test Results: each test passed, failed or skipped, a
  failed check with its values, a row that opens the failing line. Rerun Failed builds again first. Debug Test at
  Caret debugs the program on CodeLLDB or GDB, filtered to the test.
- **Full jkit support.** Editora drives [jkit](https://jkit-project.dev/) for every command it has: the project's pins
  come from jkit itself (`jkit status`: `jkit.toml`, `.sdkmanrc`, `.tool-versions`, `.java-version`), **Set Project
  JDK…** can keep the choice in `jkit.toml` (`jkit pin`), and sbt and GraalVM join JDK, Maven and Gradle. New **Java
  Toolchain** commands sync the project (`jkit sync`), show jkit's status, check its setup (`jkit doctor`), remove
  older builds (`jkit prune`), browse installs, set jkit's default vendors and switching on `cd` (`jkit config`), add
  jkit's hook to your shell, and update jkit. **Settings → Build Tools → jkit** names the jkit program and opens jkit's
  own settings; Doctor has a jkit row.
- **Run File runs single-file Java programs.** A `.java` outside a Maven or Gradle project whose first class has a
  `static void main(String[] args)` gets a ▶ on that `main`, and Run File runs it with the source launcher
  (`java Hello.java`): no project, no build. A `public` main runs on JDK 11 or newer; Run File says when the JDK is
  older. Until now only compact source files (a top-level `void main`) ran on their own.
- **launch.json `serverReadyAction` and `postDebugTask`.** A configuration's `serverReadyAction` watches the
  program's output for the server's address (VS Code's pattern and `uriFormat`), then opens it in the browser, debugs
  it in Chrome or Edge beside the server, or starts another configuration; `killOnServerStop` stops that session with
  the server. Its `postDebugTask` runs when the session ends, and before the launch again on Restart.
- **Summary of a log.** **Log: Summarize** opens a Markdown report of the active log: its records per level, a
  records-over-time table with warnings and errors and a bar per interval, the most frequent messages counted with
  their numbers and ids masked, and the longest silences.
- **Merge logs by time.** **Log: Merge Logs…** opens two or more logs as one read-only log, their records in the order
  they were written (stack traces stay with theirs, each file keeps its own order), each line tagged with its file's
  colour and name.
- **Test Results for more test runners.** Running a test file under Jest, Vitest, Deno, RSpec, Minitest (and
  `bin/rails test`), PHPUnit, ExUnit or `dart test` fills Test Results: each test passed, failed or skipped, a
  failure's message and stack, a row that opens the test where it failed. Rerun Failed and Rerun This Test run
  just those tests with the runner's own filter. The Run console keeps the runner's usual report. Run File on a
  Dart test file now runs `dart test`.
- **Warnings and errors on a log's scrollbar.** A stripe over the scrollbar marks a log's WARN lines in amber and its
  ERROR and FATAL lines in red; hover a mark to read the line, click it to go there. A filtered log marks what the
  filter kept.
- **Times in logs.** The log viewer reads each line's timestamp (ISO, Logback, Tomcat, syslog, klog, access logs, and
  JSON `time`/`ts` fields, also as epoch numbers). **Log: Go to Time…** jumps to the first line written at or after a
  time, **Log: Filter by Time…** shows the records between two times (`10:05 - 10:20`), and **Show From/Up To Caret
  Line** set one end from the line at the caret. The control bar shows the range.
- **Live logs from containers, Kubernetes, systemd and SSH.** **Log: Open Log Stream…** opens a read-only log tab fed
  by `docker logs -f`, `kubectl logs -f`, `journalctl -f -u`, `ssh host tail -F` or any command you type, with level
  colors, filters and Follow (off pauses it). Closing the tab stops the command.
- **Compressed logs open directly.** A `.gz` file such as logrotate's `app.log.2.gz` opens decompressed and read-only,
  in the log viewer when its name is a log's, so it can be filtered without unpacking it. A large one shows its last
  16 MB (a log) or first 16 MB.
- **Logs open the way you left them.** A log remembers its level floor and its show and hide patterns, and a file's
  **View as Log** choice is kept too (also turning off a file recognised as a log by its lines), so the next session
  opens it filtered as before.
- **Hide records in the log viewer.** The log control bar has a second field, for the records to hide: a record whose
  first line matches is hidden with its stack trace, and any other matching line on its own, so `at org.springframework`
  shortens traces and `HealthCheck` drops the health checks. **Aa** makes both patterns match case, the show pattern's
  matches are highlighted in the visible lines, and **Log: Hide Matching Records** sets the pattern from the palette.
  A pattern that backtracks without end (`(a+)+$`) gives up after 50 ms a line instead of freezing the window.
  **Log: Focus Filter** and **Log: Toggle Follow** have default keys (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+L), and
  Next/Previous Problem steps through a log's warnings and errors; the CUA and Sublime keymaps bind it to F8.
- **Run Test at Caret everywhere Debug Test at Caret works.** In a Go, Rust, Dart, JavaScript/TypeScript (node:test,
  Deno, Jest, Vitest), RSpec, Minitest, PHPUnit, ExUnit or C# test file, Run Test at Caret now runs the test at the
  caret alone, without the debugger, as Run File runs the file: before, only Java and Python tests ran at the caret.
- **Homebrew and winget packages** (Pauta REL-12, REL-13, REL-14). A release now writes a Homebrew cask, for
  `brew install --cask adriandeleon/tap/editora` on Apple Silicon Macs, and opens a winget pull request for
  `winget install AdrianDeLeon.Editora` on Windows. Both need the `PACKAGES_TOKEN` repository secret; without it a
  release publishes on GitHub only, as before. A manual dry run of the release workflow renders the cask and the
  manifests without publishing.
- **Elixir.** Elixir is a language of its own: highlighting, indentation, folding, the outline, snippets and a new-file
  template, with ElixirLS as its language server. Run File and Debug File run a Mix project's tests (`mix test`), a
  script (`mix run`) or the project, and Debug Test at Caret debugs the ExUnit test at the caret alone, stopping in your
  modules with their values. ElixirLS installs from **Settings → Debugging**.
- **Ruby tests and Rails apps.** Run File and Debug File now run a Ruby file as what it is: an RSpec or Minitest file's
  tests (through `bin/rails test` in a Rails app), a Rails app's server, or a script, under `bundle exec` in a bundled
  project. Debug Test at Caret debugs the RSpec example or Minitest test at the caret alone, and F5 in a Rails
  controller serves the app so a request stops at your breakpoints.
- **Attach to a remote program.** **Debug: Attach to Remote Program…** debugs a C, C++ or Rust program running under
  gdbserver (or lldb-server) on another machine, in a container or on a board, with a copy of the program here for its
  symbols, on GDB or CodeLLDB. A launch.json `cppdbg` configuration with `miDebuggerServerAddress` attaches the same way.
- **Electron apps.** F5 on an Electron app's main file, or a file that loads `electron`, debugs the whole app: its
  main process and its windows' scripts, in two sessions started and stopped together, as VS Code's Electron
  configurations do. Run File starts the app.
- **Debugging in Firefox.** Choose Firefox under **Debug web pages in** on **Settings → Debugging** and F5 on an HTML
  file, **Debug in Browser…** and **Attach to Browser…** debug the page in Firefox, as VS Code's Debugger for Firefox
  does, with breakpoints in its scripts, stepping, values and the console. A launch.json `firefox` configuration
  launches or attaches. The Firefox debugger (vscode-firefox-debug) installs from its card on the same page.
- **PHP web apps and PHPUnit.** Run File and Debug File now run a PHP file as what it is: a script, a web app's
  `index.php` on PHP's built-in web server, a Laravel app as `artisan serve` serves it, or a PHPUnit test file's tests.
  Debugging a web app stops at your breakpoints on each request, and F5 in any class file of the app serves it. Debug
  Test at Caret debugs the PHPUnit test at the caret alone. **Debug: Listen for Xdebug** waits for PHP you start
  yourself, such as a request to your own web server, without a launch.json.
- **Conditions on instruction breakpoints.** An instruction breakpoint in the Disassembly view can now have a
  condition and a hit count (Edit Breakpoint… on its row), as a line breakpoint can, where the debugger takes them
  (CodeLLDB, GDB, Delve). The Breakpoints list shows the session's instruction breakpoints too: Enter opens the
  Disassembly view at one, Alt+D removes it.
- **Autos.** When the program stops, the Debug window's Variables view now has an **Autos** list at its end: open it
  to see the values of the variables and fields used on the line it stopped at and the line before, as Visual Studio
  shows them. It stays open from stop to stop once you open it, and works with every debugger Editora runs.
- **Kotlin and Groovy tests at the caret.** Kotlin and Groovy test files in a Gradle or Maven project get the blue ▶ on
  each test, Run Test at Caret and Debug Test at Caret, as Java's have: JUnit tests (Kotlin's `` `named like this` ``
  ones too), Spock features (`def "adds two numbers"()`) and Kotest specs (run as a whole). Debugging one stops at
  your breakpoints in the Kotlin or Groovy source, and Test Results opens the test's file.
- **Return values after a step.** When a step leaves a function, the Variables view shows what it returned, first
  in the caller's locals as `(return) name`. It works in Python, and in Kotlin, Groovy and Clojure on Editora's own
  JVM debugger, for the function you step out of (JavaScript's debugger shows its own "Return value").
- **Jest and Vitest.** In a package that tests with Jest or Vitest, Debug Test at Caret now debugs the test (or
  `describe`) at the caret under that runner, alone, with breakpoints in your test and the code it calls, TypeScript
  and `.tsx` files included. F5 on a test file debugs all of its tests, and Run File on it runs them with the runner
  instead of `node --test`. Editora uses the runner installed in the package's `node_modules`.
- **Lua debugging.** Press F5 on a Lua script to debug it: breakpoints (with conditions), locals, upvalues and
  globals, watches and hovers, stepping, changing a variable's value, and a stop where an error is raised. The script's
  output appears in the Debug console. It runs on Local Lua Debugger, which Settings ▸ Debugging ▸ Lua installs (it
  needs Node.js), with the `lua` on your PATH (or `lua5.4`, `lua5.3`, `luajit`…). launch.json `lua-local`
  configurations work too. A launch.json `bashdb` configuration, which started nothing before, now starts as well.
- **Deno.** A JavaScript or TypeScript file in a Deno project (a folder with a `deno.json` or `deno.jsonc`) now
  runs under Deno: Run File runs `deno run` (a test file `deno test`) from the project's folder, with every
  permission granted, since the Run console can't ask for them. F5 debugs it the same way through the JavaScript
  debugger: breakpoints in your TypeScript, locals, watches and stepping. Debug Test at Caret runs just the
  `Deno.test` (or `describe`) around the caret. A file whose first line names `deno` (`#!/usr/bin/env -S deno run`)
  debugs too. Editora finds Deno on your PATH or in `~/.deno/bin`, where its installer puts it.
- **The documentation comes with Editora.** Help ▸ Documentation now opens the user guide that ships inside
  Editora, in your browser: the same pages as the website, with their pictures, search and every command's page,
  for the version you are running, and without a network connection. Help for a command in the palette, Settings'
  *Help for* links and Pauta Conformance open it too. Links to pages it does not hold, such as News, go to the
  website, and the new Help ▸ Online Documentation opens the website's copy.
- **Debug Test at Caret for Dart.** In a Dart `_test.dart` file, Debug Test at Caret debugs the `test`,
  `testWidgets` or `group` the caret is in, alone, on Dart's (or Flutter's) test runner; outside them, every test of
  the file.
- **Dart and Flutter.** Editora now knows Dart: syntax colouring, comments, indenting and folding, the
  Structure panel and Go to Symbol, snippets, a New File template and its file icon. With the Dart SDK (or
  Flutter's) installed, Dart's own analysis server gives errors, completion, navigation, rename and formatting
  (Settings ▸ Language Servers ▸ Dart); in a folder you haven't trusted it waits when the package names analyzer
  plugins, which run its code. Run File on a Dart file with a `main` runs `dart run` in its package's folder; on a
  Flutter app's file it runs `flutter run` on this computer's desktop, or on the device named in Settings ▸
  Debugging ▸ Dart. F5 debugs either on the SDK's own debugger (`dart debug_adapter`, `flutter debug_adapter`):
  breakpoints, conditions and logpoints, locals, watches and hovers, and stops on uncaught exceptions (or on every
  exception). Dart run configurations run and debug the same way.
- **Edit memory in the Memory view.** While the program is paused, double-click a row of the Debug window's Memory
  view (or press F2, or use its right-click menu's Edit Bytes…) and type new bytes, in hex or as "quoted text". Only
  the bytes you changed are written, and the view and the Variables view show the new values. It works on CodeLLDB,
  GDB and Delve (C, C++, Rust and Go). The Memory view also finds a C array's bytes on GDB now, where typing its name
  said it had no address.
- **Instruction breakpoints.** In the Debug window's Disassembly view, click the margin before an instruction's
  address, press F9, or use the row's right-click menu to put a breakpoint on that one machine instruction. The
  program stops there, and the Disassembly view opens at it. It works on CodeLLDB, GDB and Delve (C, C++, Rust and
  Go). The breakpoints last for the debug session, since an address belongs to that run of the program.
- **Run and debug Django, Flask and FastAPI apps.** Run or Debug a Django project's `manage.py` and its development
  server starts (`runserver`); do the same on a Flask or FastAPI app's file and Editora serves it with
  `flask run --reload` or `uvicorn --reload`, from the right folder. Breakpoints in your views stop, and keep
  stopping after you edit a file and the server reloads: the debugger follows the reloader into each new server
  process. Add (and Save as Run Configuration) proposes the server as a run configuration, and Python run
  configurations, scripts and modules alike, can now be debugged, with their interpreter, options and variables.
- **A System theme that follows your light or dark setting.** Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Theme (and Set App Theme in
  the Command Palette) now starts with System: Editora Light while your system is light, Editora Dark while it is
  dark, and it switches as soon as the system does, without a restart. The editor theme follows it on Automatic,
  and can be set to System on its own too.
- **High Contrast Light and High Contrast Dark.** A pair of app and editor themes with black or white grounds, and
  text, accents, states and syntax colours that read at 7:1 or better. Pick one like any theme; while Windows'
  high-contrast mode is on, Editora switches to it by itself (the light or the dark one, as the Windows scheme
  is), and goes back to your theme when the mode ends.
- **Ctrl/Cmd-hover shows what Ctrl/Cmd-click follows.** Hold Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) over code and the symbol under
  the mouse is underlined, and the pointer becomes a hand, when Go to Definition can take you somewhere from
  there: a symbol the language server resolves, or an HTML page's `href`/`src`. Click to go, as before; let go of
  the key and the link goes away. VS Code and IntelliJ show the same.
- **Run `.http` files from the command line.** `editora http api.http` runs every request of the file, in order,
  as Run All does — same cookie jar, chained responses, `# @assert` checks and JavaScript handlers — and prints
  each response and test, for CI and scripts. Like JetBrains' `ijhttp`: `--env dev`, `--env-file`,
  `--private-env-file`, `-V name=value` (and `-P` for one masked in the output), `-L HEADERS` or `VERBOSE`,
  `--report` for a JUnit XML report, `--no-scripts`. It exits 1 when a request fails or a test fails.
  `editora http --help` lists everything.
- **A command line on Windows.** The Windows install has a console launcher, `editora-cli.exe`, beside
  `Editora.exe`, and the MSI now puts Editora's folder on the PATH (and takes it off on uninstall). So
  `editora-cli http api.http`, `editora-cli --version` and `editora-cli --help` print in the terminal and
  return their exit status, and `editora file.txt` opens a file from any terminal.
- **A project's own JDK, Maven and Gradle, from its `.sdkmanrc`.** A project with an `.sdkmanrc`
  (`java=21.0.9-tem`, `maven=3.9.11`, `gradle=8.14.3`) now builds, runs, debugs and is analysed by the Java
  language server on that JDK, and builds with that Maven or Gradle when it has no wrapper, instead of the one
  Default JDK in Settings. A project can also name them in `.editora/settings.json` (`"toolchain": {"jdk":
  "21"}`), which wins in a trusted folder. Java Toolchain: Set Project JDK… (and Maven, Gradle) picks one from
  every install on the machine and asks whether to keep it in `.sdkmanrc` or Editora's project settings. Gradle
  runs on the project's JDK when it names one. When the project names something that is not installed, Editora
  says so once.
- **jkit support.** Editora finds every JDK, Maven and Gradle [jkit](https://jkit-project.dev) installed
  (`~/.jkit`, or `JKIT_HOME`), for the Java language server, Run and Debug, the Default JDK list and remote hosts,
  and drives jkit from Tools ▸ Java Toolchain: install the JDK, Maven and Gradle the project names, install
  another JDK from any vendor, upgrade every install to its newest build, make one jkit's default, and remove
  one. Driving jkit needs a jkit with `--json`.
- **Run File runs C, C++, Go and Rust files.** A file with a program's `main` — a lone C or C++ file, one of a CMake or
  Make project, a Go file of `package main` (or a Go test file), a Rust file of a Cargo package — gets the gutter ▶
  and Run File, as Python and shell scripts do. It is built the way Debug File builds it (`cc -g -O0` for a lone C
  file, the project's own build otherwise), and the program runs in the Run console with its output and exit code.
  Before, only F5 started such a file, and Run said it was not runnable. Debug: Debug Current File now also works on
  a file that Run File runs.
- **Internal: a performance A/B against the previous release.** `scripts/perf-ab.sh <tag> [reps]` builds the
  previous release in a worktree beside the main checkout and runs a headless probe against both builds,
  interleaved: typing (including rendered frames per keystroke), scrolling, idle, highlighting, a large file, heap
  per tab, Find and save. It prints a table of medians and marks anything more than 10 % worse. Each release now
  runs it before the tag (docs/release.md, step 3).

### Changed

- **Settings shows one language at a time on Language Servers and Debugging.** Each page has a **Language** picker and
  shows only that language's cards, instead of a wall of 27 servers and 9 adapters. A search ignores the pick and
  shows every language with a hit. Go's Goroutines card now sits with Go, and Build Tools' "pom.xml editing" link opens
  Language Servers with Maven picked.
- **Run File says why a Java file does not run on its own.** On a `.java` that is neither a single-file program nor a
  compact source file (a library class, a class of a Maven or Gradle project), Run File now says what runs as one
  file and that a project class's `main` runs from its ▶. Its other "Not a runnable file" message no longer lists a
  few languages of the many it runs.
- **Typing allocates about two thirds less.** Each keystroke in a 2,000-line Java file made the UI thread allocate
  about 7 MB, and now about 2.4 MB, so the garbage collector runs less often while you type. The editor's scrolling
  layer (Flowless, now a vendored fork like RichTextFX) measured every visible line again on each layout pass and
  rebuilt its size index whenever a line was restyled, even though the line's size had not changed; it now keeps the
  size when the line measures the same.
- **Faster typing, startup and large projects** (performance review of 2026-11-23).
  - Typing renders about a third fewer frames (3.7 → 2.6 per key) and takes about half the UI-thread time: the
    overlays drawn over the text share one look at where it is per frame instead of each measuring it again on the
    next three frames. Scrolling with pinned scope headers no longer measures them again on every step, and fold
    detection, the minimap and the spell checker's code-line scan share the editor's one typing-pause timer.
  - A tab in the background no longer keeps a full-window texture for each overlay that had painted, such as the
    indent guides and the minimap: 30 open tabs used about 145 MB for them, and memory per tab is back to what it
    was in October.
  - A typing pause no longer copies the whole document on the UI thread: highlighting, folding, TODO, spell, Run
    and Markdown scans build their text in the background. Markdown no longer copies and scans the document on every
    keystroke, typing a tag name in HTML or XML no longer copies it for each letter, CSV rainbow colours restyle only
    the records an edit changed, Git blame measures each distinct author and date once, unchanged TODO marks are not
    pushed again, and Ctrl/Cmd-click on an HTML link without a language server no longer parses the page on the UI
    thread.
  - Start-up builds each menu's items when that menu first opens, builds the Project Map when it is first opened
    rather than with the Project panel, and reads the AI keys from the keychain and decodes the window icons while
    other start-up work goes on.
  - A window no longer builds a tooltip for every button, status bar item and tab before it first paints: each
    tooltip is built the first time the pointer rests on its control, and looks and reads the same as before.
  - Nor does it build a right-click menu for every tool-window button and tab, the toolbar, the breakpoint gutter
    and the debugger's value popup: each is built when it is first opened, from the mouse or the keyboard.
  - Project Map: typing in a column filter on a very large folder no longer sorts the whole map per keystroke;
    zooming, and with Compact rows moving the pointer between columns, no longer re-sorts or lays out every column;
    problem counts are no longer rebuilt every 100 ms while the Map is hidden; "Show dependencies of the selection"
    works the overlay out off the UI thread and remembers recent ones; painting no longer allocates row-sized arrays
    per frame, and expanding a folder no longer re-measures every label.
  - Git: the Commit window keeps its rows for an unchanged status, catches up when shown, and restores the selection
    in linear time. Switching tabs or saving shortly after a Git refresh diffs only the active file, with a full
    `git status` within 2 s; files a build creates or deletes no longer run `git status` up to four times a second,
    and changes wholly inside gitignored folders skip Git. Rollback or Discard of many files writes the Local
    History index once. Coming back to the window checks folder times instead of re-walking the project's file list.
  - Language servers: the Problems window updates only the files whose problems changed; ESLint checks a JS/TS file
    2 s after typing stops (was 0.8 s) and reuses the configuration it found instead of starting Node.js at every
    short pause; after an autosave, the recheck of the other open Java files waits for a 5 s lull; a Ctrl/Cmd-hover
    probe for a new word cancels the last; inlay hints equal to those shown no longer re-lay out the lines.
  - Debugger: a stop or step fetches the top 50 frames, not 1,000 (the Call Stack's last row lists the rest); a
    stop's frame files are checked once each, off the adapter's reader thread (much faster over SSH); breakpoint
    filters, token logpoints, exception-breakpoint checks, step filters and Thread Dump's pause no longer make the
    Debug window flicker between Running and Suspended; a Python exception breakpoint for built-in types no longer
    stops the program on every raised exception; Debug History keeps at most 4 KB of each value; multi-line values
    are drawn without splitting the whole value.
  - Consoles and tools: the Run console draws a fast `\r` progress counter as one update per output burst; an open
    console find bar searches only new output, and nothing with an empty query; the Test Results tree updates its
    rows in place during a run; the CSV grid parses off the UI thread and keeps its columns when they don't change;
    Mermaid diagrams in the Markdown preview and agent replies no longer start a renderer for every version of a fence
    being typed or streamed, and a code fence still streaming in an agent reply is highlighted once it closes.
  - Second pass: start-up paints the first file about 10% sooner (the find bar's buttons are built when Find first
    opens, the editor component and fonts are prepared while the settings load, and independent settings files are
    read side by side; the minimap draws just after the file instead of delaying its first frame). Typing renders
    about a third fewer frames again (1.87 → 1.29 per key on a short line, 2.58 → 1.58 on a long one): finding where
    a character is on screen no longer costs an extra frame, and the column ruler, the status bar's line and column
    and the scrollbar marks no longer redraw in a frame of their own after each key.
  - After a branch switch or a large outside change, the symbol index re-reads only the files that changed, and Go to
    Symbol and Go to Definition answer at once while it refreshes. The project watcher no longer re-reads the build
    files to find the Java style folders on every change.
  - Local History no longer re-checks the permissions of every stored revision at each start, and its folder view no
    longer merges every project's history and checks every listed file on each tab switch.
  - Language servers: the Problems window builds a row's menu when you open it; new inlay hints and code lenses
    re-lay out only the lines that changed, once; hovering a code lens no longer walks the whole editor; Java semantic
    highlighting keeps its tokens compact and decodes them off the server's reader thread; Java diagnostics no longer
    look for the build folder on disk at each update; the Project Map's usage counts stop asking for references as
    soon as you type again.
  - Debugging: Kotlin, Groovy, Scala and Clojure fetch a stop's call stack in one request and look for each source
    file once; starting a session no longer copies every open tab; typing above a breakpoint no longer re-reads and
    compares the whole file at each newline; Variables at an earlier stop in Debug History and the session tabs with
    several sessions update faster.
  - Diffs, Resolve Conflicts, writing a diff-view edit back and the debugger's line mapping no longer spend seconds on
    two texts that share little: past 4,000 line edits they use the coarse comparison. The HTTP response viewer
    formats only the part of a large JSON body it shows. Finishing a long agent reply keeps the parts already shown.
    A new colour swatch in a CSS or HTML file no longer restyles the whole editor.
  - Local History: with a long history, a save no longer rewrites the whole history index. It writes a small file of
    what changed beside it (an 8.8 MB index: 42 ms and 8.8 MB written per save → about 1 ms and 13 KB), and the index
    is rewritten every ten minutes or so of saving, when that file grows, and at quit. A crash keeps every saved
    version, and two Editoras on one configuration folder still keep each other's versions and deletions.
- **Editora's Linux app ID is now `io.github.adriandeleon.Editora`** (it was `com.editora.Editora`), as Pauta asks.
  It is the ID GNOME Software, KDE Discover and other software centres know Editora by. The listing says it replaces
  the old ID, and an upgrade removes the file named for the old one, so Editora is listed once.
- **Local History keeps more, and says more.** Git Rollback and Discard of tracked files now keep a Local History
  copy of each file first, and nothing is discarded when a copy can't be made, so a change made outside Editora and
  never committed can be brought back. Maven Update Versions keeps a copy of a closed `pom.xml` before rewriting it,
  Decrypt to File keeps a copy of the file it replaces, and Save as Administrator keeps the version it replaced.
  Rows now say what came before them: *Before agent write*, *Before HTTP response*, *Before restore*, *Before revert*
  and *Before link update*, where they all used to read *External change*.
- **Local History's folder view.** It keeps your place (the selected version, its diff and the scroll) while files
  in the folder are saved or restored, has a filter by file name, label, reason or time, sets labels with F2, and
  deletes a file's history with Delete. After a restore, the keyboard stays in the list, for the next one.
- **Recent Changes lists this project.** Local History ▸ Recent Changes now lists the window's project only, or
  every file in a window with no project; picking a deleted file's row selects that revision in its folder's view.
- **Encrypt File and Local History.** After a file is encrypted, its banner says how many plain copies Local History
  still holds and offers to delete them.
- **Delete History of File** offers *Delete Everywhere* when Save As copies share its snapshots, so the text can
  really leave the disk; after any purge, the status says why content may still be on disk for a while (another
  running Editora, an index backup, or an index not trusted yet).
- **An LSP edit that deletes many files asks first.** When it deletes more files than Local History copies (200),
  Editora says so and asks before going ahead.
- **Editora now works toward Pauta 6.2.0** (it was 6.0.1). About and the README name the new edition. In 6.2.0 an icon
  on a menu row is optional, so menu rows without one are no longer listed as unmet.
- **Force Push is offered only after a rejected push.** The Git ▸ Remotes ▸ Force Push (with Lease) row and its
  palette command are gone. When a push is rejected because the remote branch has commits yours does not, the
  question offers Pull, then Push (the default) and, in red beside it, Force with Lease, which still refuses to
  overwrite commits you have not fetched.
- **The terminal's paste confirmation has a palette command too.** Terminal: Change a Setting… now lists
  "Confirm a paste of several lines", so it can be turned off and on from the palette as from its Settings row.
- **The menu bar is in the title bar by default on Windows and Linux.** The extended window, until now an
  experimental option, is on for new installs and for existing ones that had left it off (it was off by default,
  so an untouched setting and a deliberate off look the same). The Settings row "Merge the menu bar into the title
  bar", or View: Toggle Menu Bar in Title Bar, turns it off for the system title bar with the menu bar below it; it applies
  after a restart. macOS is unchanged: its menus stay in the system menu bar.


- **Big files keep more of the editor, from measured limits.** The size limits were set by hand; they are now
  measured, and most moved up. A file now loses highlighting, the minimap and undo at 200,000 lines (or 16 MB)
  instead of 5 MB, so a 150,000-line generated source keeps its colours while a 5 MB file of very short lines,
  which costs more memory, no longer slips through on its byte count. A long file keeps its minimap: from
  50,000 lines (was 10,000, and a stored 10,000 moves to it) only the language server stays off, unless the
  language keeps it longer. A line up to 1 MiB (was 64 KiB) keeps undo, and highlighting for the rest of the file; such
  a line still opens unwrapped, as before. A file whose document would not fit the
  free memory opens as a read-only slice, now counted by lines as well as size.
- **Settings ▸ Snippets writes a snippet file whole.** A save, a removal or switching a snippet off or on now
  writes that language's snippet file as plain JSON, so comments in it are not kept (the order of the snippets,
  every trigger, the scope and fields Editora does not use still are). A file with comments still loads, and the
  first save of one asks first, naming the file. Edit User Snippets, which opens the file as text, keeps them.
  Settings Sync merges a snippet file changed on two machines the same way.
- **A release's notes are its changelog.** The text of each GitHub release, which What's New on the Welcome page
  opens, is now this file's section for the version, after a short install guide, instead of a list of commits. A
  section too long for a release page is shown by its entries' first lines, with a link to the whole of it.
- **The Linux fat jars are signed too.** Like the `.deb`, `.rpm`, AppImage and tarball, each Linux jar now has an
  OpenPGP signature beside it (`<file>.asc`), by the key attached to the release as `editora-signing-key.asc`.

### Fixed

- **Java projects catch up after a quick checkout and pull.** When a project's `pom.xml` files changed twice within a
  second (a `git checkout` then a `git pull`), jdtls could update only some modules and leave imports of a sibling
  module red although Maven built fine. Editora now tells jdtls to update the projects again once the changed build
  files have settled.
- **Word wrap takes effect every time.** Turning word wrap on in a file with long lines sometimes wrapped nothing and
  kept the horizontal scrollbar, more often on a busy machine: a long line the view was showing again kept the width
  it was measured at unwrapped, and every line was laid out at that width.
- **Menu rows read alike.** Rows that kept their palette prefix because one word would be left ("File: Save",
  "Edit: Occur…", "Tool Window: Project", "Git: Push") have menu titles of their own ("Save", "List Matching
  Lines…", "Project", "Push"), in every language.
- **The C-x echo goes when the chord ends.** After C-x C-f or another chord the status bar kept showing "C-x -" until
  something else replaced it.
- **A new file in a folder not made yet gets its language server.** The server was started in the missing folder
  and failed to launch.
- **A question with nothing more to say has no empty band.** "Quit Editora?" with no terminal running showed a blank
  row between the question and its buttons.
- **A window closed in the first seconds of a session no longer lingers in memory.** Each open file asks for its
  spell-check dictionary (and prose completion for its word list), and the first one built in a session takes a few
  seconds; a window closed before it was ready stayed in memory (about 20 MB) until it was. It is now released at
  once.
- **Elixir language server.** ElixirLS crashed on Editora's first request and was restarted again and again, so
  Elixir files had no diagnostics, completion or hover. Editora now sends request ids as numbers, as VS Code does;
  ElixirLS refused them as strings.
- **A relative config folder stays where you started Editora.** A relative `EDITORA_CONFIG_DIR` or `--config-dir` is
  now taken relative to the folder Editora was started in, so the Java language server's workspaces are no longer
  created in whatever folder a later process runs in.
- **Colour swatches in the split view** are now drawn in their colours.
- **Git and GitHub, second review.** A second review of Git and GitHub support found about 85 problems, now fixed:
  - *Safety.* The Project Map's Changes card could run a diff program a repository's own config names; it no
    longer can. Force with Lease adds `--force-if-includes` and names the one branch it replaces, so a background
    fetch can't let it overwrite a teammate's commits, and other branches are never forced. Switching to a branch
    that was deleted elsewhere no longer restores a folder of the same name from the index. Discard on a
    `git add -N` file no longer empties it, and Discard or Revert now also reverts a file's unsaved edits (after
    saying so). Leaving a detached HEAD with commits of its own asks first from every checkout, not only the log's.
    Undo Last Commit refuses if HEAD moved while it asked.
  - *Branches and pushes.* A new branch from `origin/main` no longer tracks `origin/main`, and a branch whose
    upstream has another name is pushed to its own name. Merge and Rebase Onto carry uncommitted changes across
    (`--autostash`). Cherry-picking a merge commit asks which parent, as Revert does. Branches checked out in another
    worktree are not offered for deletion. Worktrees of a repository on a remote host work. The no-repository
    dropdown offers Initialize Repository.
  - *Refreshing.* Commits, staging and checkouts done in a terminal, and renames or deletes in the Project tree,
    now refresh the Commit window. A pre-commit hook's rewrites reload into the open files. An open Git Log
    reloads only when a branch or HEAD moved, not after every stage.
  - *Commit window.* Amend follows a moved HEAD or switches off instead of amending another commit with the old
    message, and a typed message stays with its repository. Commit saves only the staged files' buffers.
    Ctrl+Enter says why it can't commit. Staging a hunk checks the hunk's lines are still there.
  - *Prompts.* Clone, fetch, pull and push never wait for a passphrase or host-key answer in the terminal
    Editora was started from; they fail at once with ssh's message.
  - *Output.* Patches, diffs and the AI commit prompt ignore `color.diff`, `diff.noprefix` and
    `diff.mnemonicPrefix`. "All branches" in the Git Log no longer lists stash and notes commits, and a tab in an
    author's name no longer garbles a row. A searched file history cut at 5,000 commits says so.
  - *Links.* Permalinks and the GitHub window understand ssh host aliases (`git@github-work:…`) and
    `ssh.github.com:443`. Bitbucket Server and Data Center get links of their own form, and GitHub links to
    Markdown files land on the lines.
  - *GitHub.* The review form starts on Comment, not Approve, and a review from the review tab is pinned to the
    commit you looked at. PR and review bodies go to `gh` on standard input. A failed checks lookup is retried
    instead of read as "no pull request". A long CI log download no longer holds up the lists. Cancel Run asks
    first. A run awaiting approval is no longer shown as failed. An expired token on one of several hosts, or a
    SAML refusal, is explained. The filter can search GitHub when no loaded row matches.
  - Smaller fixes in blame, relative dates, the merge viewer, patch tabs, Load More errors and the remotes
    manager.
  - *A third look* at these fixes: a review from the review tab on GitHub Enterprise goes to that server, not to
    github.com. Conflicts from changes stashed by a merge or rebase are reported when it finishes, and the banner says
    they are stashed meanwhile. Commits made in a terminal on branches like `feature/x` refresh the Commit window, and
    switching to a repository in the middle of a merge keeps its merge message. Show Commit from blame works after
    unsaved edits above the line. A forced push to a Gerrit remote keeps its `refs/for/…` refspec. A desktop
    passphrase dialog (`SSH_ASKPASS`) still asks for an ssh key's passphrase. ssh aliases written with capitals
    resolve, and an expired token on one host no longer blocks a repository whose other remote is fine. Branch from
    Stash and Check Out PR ask before leaving a detached HEAD's commits behind.
  - *A fourth look:* a push to a remote with push refspecs of its own names the branch unless they push `HEAD`
    (Gerrit), so a notes or mirror refspec can no longer push something else or force every branch. Discarding a
    file with unsaved edits keeps those edits in Local History before the tab closes, and the question names the
    files. Staging while the Git Log is still loading no longer restarts it, and the log no longer waits behind a slow
    commit hook. Choosing a remote branch skips local branches checked out in another worktree. A review tab notices
    a push made while it loaded, and an Enterprise address with a port is not pinned.
- **`${fileDirnameBasename}` in `launch.json` is empty for a file at the root of a drive.** It used to read
  `null`, as did `${relativeFileDirname}` when the file had no folder; both are now empty, as in VS Code.
- **Old error underlines came back after some edits.** After signature help, Format, code actions and other requests
  that send the text first, the typing pause could put the pre-edit squiggles back on lines the edit had moved.
- **The Threads view stopped updating** while a program kept starting and ending threads.
- **Debug Test on Maven and Gradle attaches again.** Debugging a test from the editor or Test Results started the
  test with its JVM waiting for the debugger, but the debugger never attached, since the build started a moment later
  than Editora checked. It attaches now.
- **A bulk edit in a large file could lose the file's previous text.** The Local History copy taken before an edit in
  a buffer with no undo (Replace in Files, an agent or LSP edit, diff apply) was reported as kept before it reached
  the disk, so the edit went ahead even when the copy failed. The edit now waits for the copy and is refused without
  it.
- **One project's big files emptied the others' Local History.** When the newest versions of a few big files were
  over the project's size limit by themselves, every other file in the project was cut to its newest version, for
  months. Only the big files' own older versions are dropped now.
- **Local History copies that were reported missing.** A copy whose index write was folded into the next one was
  reported as failed, so an agent write, a Replace in Files on a closed file or a delete could be refused for no
  reason.
- **Local History gaps.** A plain `.asc` file (AsciiDoc, a public key) was never recorded, because encrypted files
  were recognised by name; a file shown only in part (a huge file, a trimmed log) was recorded as if that part were
  the whole file; and the version a save replaced was not kept for files over 5 MB.
- **Local History across windows and processes.** Delete History of Project and Save As now cover what every window
  recorded; a restore from the folder view of a file open in another window goes into that window's tab, asking
  first over unsaved edits; and with two Editoras on one configuration, a rename in one no longer deletes the
  other's history of that file.
- **Local History and encodings.** A version restored after the file was deleted outside Editora keeps the file's
  charset, byte-order mark and line endings; a UTF-16 file without a byte-order mark gets a copy before a restore;
  and the folder view's *Current* side shows a closed file in its own encoding.
- **The Local History window** keeps the selected version and its diff after you rename its label, and reopens when
  you come back to a file after a tab with none (it used to stay closed).
- **Local History upkeep.** A clock set ahead and then corrected no longer leaves versions that never expire; an empty
  index backup no longer stops old content being collected for 30 days, and a lost index gets the same 30-day grace as a
  damaged one.
- **A closed window no longer lingers in memory after a late GitHub check.** With the GitHub CLI installed, a window
  closed while Editora was still asking `gh` whether it is signed in got the answer afterwards: the closed window
  showed its GitHub tool window and saved its settings, and that save could keep the whole window (about 20 MB) in
  memory. The answer is now dropped once the window has closed.
- **Folding no longer stops on a very long XML or HTML tag.** A tag (or a stray `<name` in text) with a couple of
  thousand characters before its `>` made the fold scan run out of stack, and that file then had no folding at all.
- **The first file you open gets its colours sooner.** Its syntax colouring no longer waits behind the start-up
  loading of every other language's grammar.
- **Smart Type completion after `return` in a switch rule's block.** In Java, a `return` inside `case X -> { … }`
  now gets the method's return type for Smart Type completion, as it does elsewhere in the method.
- **The Disassembly view on GDB** now shows the instructions leading up to where the program stopped. GDB used to
  answer with instructions after it, so the current instruction wasn't in the list.
- **Debugger review fixes, second round.** A second review of the debugger found these, now fixed:
  - **"Don't step into" and your own code.** A filter such as `kotlin.*`, `java.*` or `scala.*` also matched your own
    `src/main/kotlin`, `src/main/java` or `src/main/scala` folder, so Step Into on your code stepped straight back
    out.
  - **The right session, after a save.** What a launch does after saving its files, or after the Run scan or a text
    scan finishes, started in whichever debug session was focused by then: a compound with unsaved files launched
    into its last session. It now starts the session that asked, and nothing once that session's tab is closed.
  - **F5 twice no longer launches twice.** Pressing F5 again while the first launch still saves or reads its plan
    says it is starting.
  - **Launches say why they stop.** A launch whose project files cannot be read (a remote host gone) says so instead
    of looking again forever; a plan that fails says why; a file edited while it saved says to debug it again.
  - **Breakpoints.** Undo after deleting a breakpoint's line brings back that breakpoint, not another on an
    identical line (two breakpoints with one id); an old deleted breakpoint no longer comes back on an unrelated
    paste; breakpoints edited in files with no tab while Mute is on are no longer lost on Unmute; a gutter click is
    not dropped when the text changes again.
  - **Debug Test** attaches only its own JVMs in its session; run configurations attach where they are started.
  - **Exceptions.** An exception stop's card and details are no longer lost when the stack goes through a file
    edited since the launch.
  - **Finding adapters and programs.** debugpy and js-debug installed by Editora are found with `--config-dir`; a
    debugger path pasted with quotes works; Attach to Process recognises Linux programs with glibc or LLVM `__`
    sections; a project opened through a symbolic link gets its Java source folder fixed again.
  - **Go** no longer deletes the program another window's long Go session runs; a stopped session's program is
    removed when it ends.
  - **Values.** Type renderers work with `f"{self.x}"`, `` `${this.x}` `` and C++ `this->x`; inline values no longer
    show the module's variable on a function's header line; pinned values beyond the 40 evaluated at once are not
    left showing another frame's; View as Table keeps a Python dict's string keys beside its integer ones, and Load
    more after a step reloads instead of mixing two stops.
  - **Smaller ones.** Windows shell tasks with a quoted command and last argument run; a Gradle project naming its own
    JDK (`.sdkmanrc`) runs and debugs on it; auto template breakpoints no longer read local files for a remote Python
    session; a Node launch whose planning fails says so; Debug Current File waits for the Run scan of a file just
    opened; Debug History stays quick on long histories; the session log file is capped.
- **On macOS, About and Settings are in the application menu, and Quit is Editora's own.** About Editora and
  Settings… open from the application menu, as on other Mac apps. Quit from that menu, Cmd-Q, the Dock or a logout
  now goes through Editora's Quit, which asks once about unsaved work, instead of closing each window in turn.
- **Debugging a C, C++ or Rust program on CodeLLDB reports the program's own exit code.** The Debug console said
  "Process finished with exit code 143" (and the status bar 143) after a program that exited 0. Recent CodeLLDB
  (1.12) has Editora start its launcher, `codelldb-launch`, and ends that launcher with SIGTERM once the program has
  exited; its 143 was reported as the program's. The program's code now comes from CodeLLDB's own exit event.

### Security

- **AI API keys are never written to settings.json.** Without a system keychain (a Linux session with no Secret
  Service, `-Deditora.secretStore=none`, or a keychain that refuses a write) the keys were kept in `settings.json`
  as plain text. They now go to an encrypted file of their own, `~/.editora/keys/secrets.enc` (AES-256-GCM, under a
  random key Editora generates in `keys/secrets.key`; the folder and both files are readable by you alone where the
  file system has permissions). A key an older version left in `settings.json`, or in a backup of it beside it, is
  moved there on the next launch and blanked; keys typed while the keychain did not answer move into it once it
  does. Export Configuration and Settings sync never carry the keys, so Export no longer asks about them. A file
  that does not decrypt is reported in Settings → AI and read as no keys; it is moved aside, never written over,
  when a key is saved. Saving a key from Settings no longer writes the keychain on the interface thread.
